title: Free time: relaxation and leisure
title_uz: Bo‘sh vaqt: dam olish va hordiq

words.ex: It only takes two hours every Saturday, but volunteering at the animal shelter in Yunusabad is the most rewarding thing I do: I come home feeling I've really made a difference.
Our partnership with a school in Termez has been very fruitful: together we've recorded a twenty-episode podcast series.
Baking birthday cakes to order started as a hobby for Feruza, but it has become so lucrative that she now earns more from it than from her teaching job.
The rehabilitation centre teaches carpet weaving because the doctors find it therapeutic for patients recovering from long illnesses.
After a week of exams, a slow walk through the botanical garden was exactly the relaxing break I needed.
Whenever I'm nervous before a test, my mother makes me a cup of mint tea; it has a calming effect, and my hands stop shaking.
Editing the school newspaper is far more time-consuming than I expected; proofreading alone leaves me barely any time for homework.
A true culture vulture, my uncle plans every trip abroad around concerts, exhibitions and old libraries rather than beaches.
Since he got a games console, my brother has turned into a real couch potato; he hasn't been outside for a walk in weeks.
Kamol plays the doira in a folk band purely as an amateur; during the day he works as an engineer.
Nodira is a bit of a dabbler: last month it was pottery, this month it's the guitar, and next month it'll probably be chess.
I can't come to the cinema until I've done my chores: washing the dishes, sweeping the yard and taking out the rubbish.
Being a real shopaholic, Zarina came home from the Samarqand Darvoza mall with three scarves she will never wear.
These days Sardor is heavily into mountain biking and spends every weekend on the trails in the hills near Parkent.
Bekzod went off football when his team lost twelve matches in a row, and now he only watches tennis.
After retiring from the bank, Mr Yusupov took up calligraphy, and now his work hangs in a small gallery in Kokand.
Before the maths olympiad, Aziz locked himself away in his room for a week and solved hundreds of problems.
Since the World Cup started, my little sister has been totally hooked on collecting football stickers and swaps them at school every day.
So what did you get up to during the Navruz holidays? Did you go anywhere nice?
With concerts, birthdays and football matches, my cousin has such a hectic social life that she needs an app to keep track of it.
I'd love to help with the project, but with music lessons, football practice and exams, I've got a very full diary until Friday.
Our neighbour Mrs Rashidova is a keen participant in every community clean-up, from planting trees along the canal to painting the playground fence.
Please keep off the lawn; the new grass was only planted last week.
Every Saturday morning, Mr Karimov mows the football pitch behind the school before the matches start.
After winning the national junior title, Diyora turned professional and now earns her living from tennis.
The charity runs a support group where recovering alcoholics can talk openly about their problems.
Lola admits she is a chocaholic: there is always a bar of something sweet hidden in her desk drawer.
